__
 
• Industrial Policy of 1956

 
 
• Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 (IPR 1956) is a resolution adopted by the Indian Parliament in April 1956.
 
• It was the first comprehensive statement on the industrial development of India. 
 
• It was regarded as the “Economic Constitution of India” or “The Bible of State Capitalism”.
 
• The government revised its first Industrial Policy (i.e.the policy of 1948) through the Industrial Policy of 1956.
 
• The 1956 Policy empha­sised the need to expand the public sector, to build up a large and growing coop­erative sector and to encourage the separation of ownership and management in private in­dustries and, above all, prevent the rise of pri­vate monopolies.
 
• It provided the basic framework for the government’s policy regarding in­dustries till June 1991.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974)** aimed to achieve a growth rate of 5.7% per annum and focused on the development of agriculture, industry, and infrastructure.
 
• **The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)** was based on the Mahalanobis model of economic development and aimed to achieve a growth rate of 4.5% per annum. It focused on heavy industries, particularly steel, and aimed to reduce the dependence on imports.
 
• **The Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985)** aimed to achieve a growth rate of 5.2% per annum and focused on poverty alleviation, employment generation, and rural development.
 
• **The Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002-2007)** aimed to achieve a growth rate of 8% per annum and focused on human development, infrastructure development, and regional development.

questions.question: From which Five - Year Plan period was the formulation and implementation of the Five - Year Plan discontinued by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Twelfth Five - Year Plan**__.

__
 
• The Government of India discontinued the formulation of Five-Year Plans after the Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–2017).
 
• This decision marked a significant shift in the planning process, transitioning from centralized planning to a decentralized framework.
 
• The NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission in January 2015, signaling the end of the Five-Year Plan era.
 
• The Twelfth Five-Year Plan focused on "Faster, More Inclusive, and Sustainable Growth" but was the last of its kind as the government moved towards rolling plans and sector-specific strategies.
 
• The discontinuation reflected a modern approach to policy-making, emphasizing flexibility and real-time monitoring over rigid long-term plans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planning Commission:**

 
 
• Established in 1950, it was responsible for drafting Five-Year Plans based on India's economic priorities.
 
• It was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015 to promote a bottom-up approach to planning.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• Formed on January 1, 2015, it serves as a policy think tank for the Government of India.
 
• It focuses on cooperative federalism, involving states in the planning process.
 
 
 
• **Rolling Plans:**
 
 
• Introduced as a replacement for Five-Year Plans, they allow for flexibility and periodic adjustments based on real-time needs.
 
• These plans focus on sector-specific growth strategies rather than a fixed timeline.
 
 
 
• **History of Five-Year Plans in India:**
 
 
• The first Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951, focusing on agriculture and irrigation.
 
• A total of 12 plans were implemented, with priorities shifting to industry, infrastructure, and social sectors over time.

questions.question: Which of the following years were considered plan holidays in Independent India?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Period:** Plan Holidays occurred from 1966 to 1969.
 
• **Reason:** The failure of the Third Five-Year Plan due to economic crises like wars and drought.
 
• **Focus:** Emphasis was placed on agriculture and price stabilization instead of long-term planning.
 
• **Result:** Short-term plans were implemented to address immediate economic issues before resuming regular Five-Year Plans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Economic Impact:** These events caused food shortages, inflation, and a balance of payments crisis, forcing the government to temporarily halt long-term planning.
 
• **Interim Plans:** During the Plan Holidays, the government implemented Annual Plans focusing on critical sectors like agriculture, irrigation, and employment creation to stabilize the economy.
 
• **Resumption:** The Fourth Five-Year Plan (**1969–1974**) resumed after these Plan Holidays, aiming to promote growth and self-reliance in the economy.

• The Planning Commission was established in March 1950 to promote a rapid rise in the standard of living of the people by efficient exploitation of the resources of the country.

• It aimed at ensuring an increase in the output of goods and services, to improve the living standards of the people.

• The Commission was headed by the Prime Minister of India and had a Deputy Chairman, appointed by the Prime Minister.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) focused on the agricultural sector, and aimed to address the immediate problem of food shortages and inflation.
 
• In 2014, the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India), which serves as the policy think tank of the Government of India.
 
• The NITI Aayog aims to involve the states in economic policy-making in India and to promote cooperative federalism.

questions.question: On which date was the National Development Council set up?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**6th August 1952**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Development Council (NDC)** was set up on **6th August 1952** by a resolution of the Government of India.
 
• The NDC is an important part of the **planning process** in India and plays a key role in the approval of plans formulated by the **Planning Commission** (now replaced by the NITI Aayog).
 
• It serves as the highest decision-making authority for **socio-economic planning in India**.
 
• The council includes the **Prime Minister of India, Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all States and Union Territories, and members of the Planning Commission**.
 
• The primary objective of the NDC is to promote **cooperation between the central and state governments** and to ensure the implementation of national plans effectively.
 
• It also reviews the progress of plans and suggests measures to achieve the objectives of **rapid economic development** and **balanced regional growth**.
 
• The establishment of the NDC marks a significant step in the development of **decentralized planning** and the involvement of states in national policy-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planning Commission**:

 
 
• The **Planning Commission**, established in **1950**, was responsible for formulating India's five-year plans.
 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** in **2015**.
 
• Its role was to assess resources, formulate strategies for economic growth, and allocate resources effectively.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**:
 
 
• The **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) is a **policy think tank** established by the Government of India in **2015**.
 
• It replaced the Planning Commission to foster a more decentralized and participative approach to governance.
 
• It focuses on **policy formulation**, fostering **cooperative federalism**, and enhancing innovation and research.

questions.question: Which of the Five-Year Plans was prepared and launched by DP Dhar?

questions.question:
In which Five-year plan was the following statement quoted?

“The urge to bring economic and social change under present conditions comes from the fact of poverty and inequalities in income, wealth and opportunity”.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First Five-year plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The statement "The urge to bring economic and social change under present conditions comes from the fact of poverty and inequalities in income, wealth, and opportunity" was quoted in the context of the **First Five-Year Plan** in India.
 
• This plan, spanning from **1951 to 1956**, emphasized **economic development and the eradication of poverty **through a centralized planning approach.
 
• It aimed to address socioeconomic disparities and lay the foundation for India's industrialization and modernization.
 
• The First Five Year Plan delineated the trajectory of economic development in India, spearheading significant initiatives.
 
• Presented by India's inaugural Prime Minister, **Jawaharlal Nehru,** it was formally introduced to the Parliament of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Second Five-Year Plan** placed a strong emphasis on rapid industrialization and the expansion of the public sector. It was formulated under the guidance of renowned economist P.C. Mahalanobis.
 
• **The Third Five-Year Plan**, implemented from 1961 to 1966, marked a shift towards a centralized and comprehensive national economic strategy aimed at fostering development across various sectors.
 
• **The Fourth Five-Year Plan**, spanning from 1969 to 1974, was structured based on the Gadgil Formula. This plan aimed to promote economic growth while ensuring stability and self-reliance. Its objectives included the development of agriculture, industry, and infrastructure to foster balanced and sustainable progress.
